title: Prince Iwakura Tomomi
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; public domain in the US. The photographer is not named in the book; a photograph of the 1870s–80s is out of copyright everywhere on any measure.
original_holder: J. Morris, Makers of Japan (London: Methuen; Chicago: A. C. McClurg, 1906)
caption: Iwakura Tomomi, the court noble who led the 1871–73 embassy to the United States and Europe, in Western-style court uniform with a sash and order. The date of the photograph is not known, and it is not one of the pictures taken on the embassy's journey; he died in 1883.

title: Marquis Kido
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; public domain in the US. The photographer is not named in the book; a photograph of the 1870s–80s is out of copyright everywhere on any measure.
original_holder: J. Morris, Makers of Japan (London: Methuen; Chicago: A. C. McClurg, 1906)
caption: Kido Takayoshi, one of the four vice-ambassadors and the embassy's most candid diarist, standing in a Western suit in a photographer's studio. The book does not say when or where the picture was taken; he died in 1877. The title 'Marquis' is the book's own; the marquisate went to his heir after his death.

title: Viscount Okubo Toshimichi
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; public domain in the US. The photographer is not named in the book; a photograph of the 1870s–80s is out of copyright everywhere on any measure.
original_holder: J. Morris, Makers of Japan (London: Methuen; Chicago: A. C. McClurg, 1906)
caption: Ōkubo Toshimichi, vice-ambassador and finance minister, bearded and in embroidered court uniform. He and Itō were sent back across the Pacific in 1872 to fetch full powers for treaty talks the embassy turned out not to be authorised to hold. The date of the photograph is not given; he was assassinated in 1878.

title: Ito Hirobumi
creator: Unknown photographer (halftone)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; public domain in the US. The photographer is not named in the book; a photograph of the 1870s–80s is out of copyright everywhere on any measure.
original_holder: David Murray, The Story of Japan (Story of the Nations; London: T. Fisher Unwin / New York: G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1894; this printing 1896)
caption: Itō Hirobumi, the youngest vice-ambassador and the embassy's English speaker, who gave its much-reported speech in San Francisco in January 1872. The portrait shows him in court dress, probably some years after the embassy; the book gives no date or photographer.

title: Jeddo and Belfast; or, A Puzzle for Japan
creator: John Tenniel (cartoon for Punch)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: James Parton, Caricature and Other Comic Art in All Times and Many Lands (New York: Harper & Brothers, 1877); cartoon first published in Punch, 1872
caption: A Punch cartoon by John Tenniel from 1872, when the embassy was in Britain. The Japanese envoy asks the Archbishop of Canterbury whether the people rioting behind banners reading 'Protestantism' and 'Catholicism' are heathen. 'On the contrary, your Excellency; those are among our most enthusiastic religionists.' It is a caricature, and its joke is aimed at British sectarian violence (the Belfast riots of that summer), not at the visitors.

title: Townsend Harris
creator: Unknown engraver
date: Published 1906 (portrait of Harris in old age; he died 1878)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: Richard Hildreth, "Japan as It Was and Is", vol. II, ed. Ernest W. Clement (Chicago: A. C. McClurg, 1906)
caption: Townsend Harris, the first American consul-general in Japan, who negotiated the 1858 Treaty of Amity and Commerce. The 1860 embassy crossed the Pacific to exchange its ratifications in Washington. The engraving shows Harris as an old man, years after the embassy, and was printed in 1906.

title: A home by the sea, Raiatea
creator: Nicholas Senn (photograph, or photographs he collected)
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1906; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are). Senn died in 1908, so it is out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: Nicholas Senn, Tahiti, the Island Paradise (Chicago: W. B. Conkey, 1906)
caption: Thatched houses on piles at the edge of the lagoon on Raiatea, Mai's home island, photographed around 1903. It is a modern photograph, not a picture of the 1770s; Mai's family land on Raiatea had been taken by conquerors from Bora Bora, and Cook would not help him win it back.

title: Tahiti from the harbor of Papeete
creator: Nicholas Senn (photograph, or photographs he collected)
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1906; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are). Senn died in 1908, so it is out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: Nicholas Senn, Tahiti, the Island Paradise (Chicago: W. B. Conkey, 1906)
caption: The mountains of Tahiti seen from the harbour of Papeete around 1903, with steamers and sailing ships at anchor. Cook's ships, with Mai aboard, lay at Matavai Bay a few miles along this coast in 1777; Papeete itself grew up later.

title: View of Moorea
creator: Nicholas Senn (photograph, or photographs he collected)
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1906; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are). Senn died in 1908, so it is out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: Nicholas Senn, Tahiti, the Island Paradise (Chicago: W. B. Conkey, 1906)
caption: The jagged peaks of Moorea, Tahiti's neighbour island, photographed around 1903. In October 1777 Cook's men, with Mai taking part, burned houses and canoes here over a stolen goat. The book does not say which bay the view is taken from.

title: "V'la les restes de notre Révolution de Juillet"
creator: Auguste Hervieu (drawn and etched)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: Frances Trollope, Paris and the Parisians in 1835, vol. II (London: Richard Bentley, 1836)
caption: 'There lie the remains of our July Revolution': a Paris workman shows a child the railed graves of fighters killed in July 1830, hung with flags, near the Louvre. Hervieu drew it about five years after the fighting that Tahtawi watched from Paris, for a book by the English writer Frances Trollope.

title: Morning at the Tuileries
creator: Auguste Hervieu (drawn and etched)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: Frances Trollope, Paris and the Parisians in 1835, vol. I (London: Richard Bentley, 1836)
caption: A grenadier and two citizens reading newspapers under the trees of the Tuileries garden. It shows the café-and-newspaper Paris that Tahtawi described to Egyptian readers, though it was drawn in 1835, a few years after he left.

title: Charles X at Valognes: parting with the Guard
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: John S. C. Abbott, Louis Philippe (Makers of History; New York: Harper & Brothers, 1871)
caption: The deposed Charles X takes leave of his guards at Valognes in August 1830, on his way to exile from Cherbourg after the July Revolution. It is an imagined scene in a wood engraving printed in an American popular history forty years later, not an eyewitness picture.

title: Court of Honor from the Administration Building
creator: C. D. Arnold / H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1893; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are), and its photographers died long ago.
original_holder: Official Views of the World's Columbian Exposition, issued by the Department of Photography, C. D. Arnold and H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers (Chicago: Press Chicago Photo-Gravure Co., 1893)
caption: The White City of the World's Columbian Exposition, Chicago, 1893: the Grand Basin, the MacMonnies fountain and the colonnade, photographed from the Administration Building. The Parliament of Religions met downtown at the new Art Institute, not on the fairground, but delegates such as Vivekananda and Dharmapala toured the fair.

title: The Japanese Ho-o-den
creator: C. D. Arnold / H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1893; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are), and its photographers died long ago.
original_holder: Official Views of the World's Columbian Exposition, issued by the Department of Photography, C. D. Arnold and H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers (Chicago: Press Chicago Photo-Gravure Co., 1893)
caption: The Hōōden ('Phoenix Hall'), the pavilion Japan's government built on the Wooded Island for the 1893 fair, modelled on the Byōdō-in near Kyoto. It was Japan's own picture of itself at the fair, which the Japanese Buddhist delegates to the Parliament, among them Shaku Sōen, could see.

title: The Ceylon Building
creator: C. D. Arnold / H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1893; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are), and its photographers died long ago.
original_holder: Official Views of the World's Columbian Exposition, issued by the Department of Photography, C. D. Arnold and H. D. Higinbotham, official photographers (Chicago: Press Chicago Photo-Gravure Co., 1893)
caption: Ceylon's carved-wood pavilion at the 1893 Chicago fair, built by the colonial government with Sinhalese craftsmen. Anagarika Dharmapala, who came from Colombo to speak for Buddhism at the Parliament, was the best-known Ceylonese voice in Chicago that year.
